correctness.rationale: The exact EBSH CDF is sinh(a(1-exp(-x^alpha))^theta)/sinh(a), a=pi/2, alpha,theta>0. Put u=exp(-x^alpha). The two Taylor expansions (1-u)^theta=1-theta*u+O(u^2) and sinh(a(1-theta*u+O(u^2)))=sinh(a)-a*theta*cosh(a)*u+O(u^2) give S(x)~(a*theta*coth(a))*exp(-x^alpha). Differentiating the published exact density supplies f(x)~C_theta*alpha*x^(alpha-1)*exp(-x^alpha); their ratio gives h(x)~alpha*x^(alpha-1). Direct exponential-integral comparison of exp(tx-x^alpha) gives the exact MGF trichotomy, including divergence at t=1 for alpha=1; log S(x+y)-log S(x) tends to zero for 0<alpha<1. Integrating powers and inverting the quantile give all positive polynomial moments and Q(1-q)~(log 1/q)^(1/alpha). Independent 80-digit evaluation of three distinct regimes corroborated all normalized asymptotic ratios; those evaluations are not the infinite proof.
residual_risks: No global hazard monotonicity is established; a terminal asymptotic cannot constrain finite x.
Heavy/light tail labels vary by discipline; the precise positive-MGF domain is unambiguous.

originality.rationale: The 27 May 2026 defining EBSH paper provides the formula but explicitly labels the whole family light-tailed because it sees an exp(-x^alpha) factor. That statement is incorrect under the positive-MGF criterion when alpha<1. The inspected survival and density sections, Section 3.1 tail paragraph, and quantile section do not supply the C_theta equivalent, hazard equivalent, or exact alpha-dependent MGF domain. The bounded parent law cannot supply unbounded-tail asymptotics. Stretched-exponential generalities predict the phase after substitution but do not themselves correct this published parameter-uniform assertion.
residual_risks: General upper-endpoint transformation theorems can imply the first-order expansion generically; this is an applied-source correction, not an independently deep asymptotic method.
A corrected preprint or later note of the journal paper might already state the same phase and affect priority.
Some applied definitions of “heavy-tailed” differ; only the mathematical MGF classification is asserted.

value.rationale: The all-light-tailed characterization is published for a model used in reliability, survival analysis and medical datasets, yet is false for the entire nonempty alpha<1 parameter region. The exact survival multiplier, the true domain of positive exponential moments, and hazard/quantile regimes together give a mathematically sharp and potentially necessary correction for selecting tail-risk models; their motivation is not merely an arbitrary asymptotic exercise.
residual_risks: The endpoint Taylor calculation is elementary and its independent novelty lies principally in identifying an actual model-specific published misclassification; no broad new theorem is claimed.

scientific_limitations: No assertion on full hazard curve or finite-sample model fit.
All alpha and theta positive and x>0; positive-exponential-moment criterion used precisely.
